_comment: The agent class restated for a policy with no end-to-end mode, exactly as mix_short_m1_slofair.json does for the static sweep: 2500 + 520.2*52 = 29,550 <= 30,000. Scoring is unaffected -- the analysis judges that class end to end whatever this says. Without it the SLO filter reads tbt_ms 25 literally, judges the agent class 2.3x tighter than FluidServe judges it, and rejects ~98% of it (EXP-28). SLO arm only: tbt_ms doubles as PolyServe's tier key.
EXP-30. One hour of Azure-shaped load with the mix cycling under it, on the
shortened agent transcript.
Why this workload exists. Every result so far was measured at a fixed rate
with a fixed mix, and both baselines are well matched to that: PolyServe's
partition is recomputed every 10 s from an EWMA with alpha 0.5 and applied
after two consecutive agreeing windows, which tracks a mix that never moves
perfectly, and the SLO filter is per-request and has no notion of the mix at
all. Measured, the partition changes once or twice in an eight-minute
condition and every change is in the start-up transient. A stationary
workload therefore cannot separate a policy that adapts from one that does
not, because nothing has to be adapted to.
What varies here, and what each part is for:
rate   25 to 75 req/s, quantile-mapped from four days of Azure conv+code
minute counts starting at 06:00, compressed 720x. The range spans
the whole region the fixed-rate sweep found: below 40 every policy
holds, at 40 PolyServe's chat class collapses, near 60 the fleet is
at its decode bound, and 75 is past it. A rate that moves is what
exercises admission control, which is the mechanism neither
baseline has -- PolyServe queues instead (549 preemptions in 8 min
at a fixed 40 req/s, about 27% of two engines' time spent
recomputing) and the Llumnix SLO arm rejects only when no instance
passes its filter.
mix    m1 -> m2 -> m3 -> m1, fifteen minutes each, stated by input-token
share against the shortened transcript. A mix that moves is what
exercises the partition. This is an OPEN question rather than a
confirmation: a 15-minute segment is far longer than PolyServe's
~30 s adaptation time, so the partition should track it, and the
cost if any is confined to the transient at each of the three
boundaries.
The two are deliberately varied together in this file and separately in
mix_dyn08_short_mixcycle.json, which holds the rate flat at 40 req/s and
cycles the mix on two-minute segments. If the flat-rate run shows no
difference between the policies and this one does, the effect is the rate,
not the mix.
The SLO block is unchanged from EXP-27 so attainment is scored on the same
rule as every run since 2026-07-27: chat 5 s / 50 ms, deep research 10 s /
100 ms, agent end-to-end 30 s (the analysis reads the agent class as an
end-to-end budget whatever ttft_ms and tbt_ms say here).
